title: Chilean night sky revealed at La Silla
caption: The Milky Way, the Moon and Jupiter over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way cuts across the night sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile, while off to the right the Moon and Jupiter shine very brightly. Below, a whole suite of telescopes stands on the mountain.
Many of those telescopes are used by ESO's Member States for targeted projects, where teams concentrate on particular scientific questions using the instruments at the site.

The sky shows objects at wildly different distances. The Moon is our closest neighbor, Jupiter is a planet in our own Solar System, and the Milky Way is the combined glow of countless distant stars in our galaxy. Through a camera they share a single frame. The brightness of the Moon and Jupiter also shows why astronomers pay attention to moonlight, since a bright Moon lights up the sky and can make faint objects harder to observe.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The Moon and Jupiter are easy to see by eye, but the long exposure makes the Milky Way much brighter than it would appear with the Moon up.
